newsitem.title: USA: Publisher fights reports over Morris book.
newsitem.headline: Publisher fights reports over Morris book.

text.p: Stung by claims that no U.S. magazine would publish advance excerpts of disgraced political guru Dick Morris's book about President Clinton, a New York publishing house took the unusual step Tuesday of making public details of the offers it received.

Random House said it had a $55,000 deal with Newsweek to publish excerpt from Morris's "Behind the Oval Office" but that deal was called off when the Washington Post and the New York Daily News last Friday ran stories on the book and, according to the publisher, "lifted quotations ... without copyright approval."

Publishing sources said it was very unusual for a publisher to reveal details of its negotiations but added that Random seemed stung by press suggestions that Morris's book was not as sensational as its advanced billing and that it was not able to arrange a deal.
More than 150,000 copies of the book went on sale Monday and sales were reported so brisk that the publisher already ordered a second printing of 25,000 copies and has plans for a third printing.
Random said that last December it rejected an offer of $20,000 from Time and instead accepted a $60,000 offer from U.S. News & World Report to publish excerpts of the book.
But last Thursday, it said it cancelled the U.S. News deal because it was not satisfied with how the magazine planned to handle the project.

It then offered the book to Newsweek, which offered $55,000. Random quoted Newsweek editor Maynard Parker as being "very interested", a point made in its news release with the apparent intent of countering a comment by Parker to the New York Times in which he said he was only "mildly interested" and was getting the book at firesale prices.
Morris was reported to have received $2.5 million for the book which he wrote after a sex scandal forced him to resign as Clinton's cihef political consultant.
His book details how he helped to reshape Clinton's presidency, moving the president to the political center and deliberately co-opting many Republican proposals.
